messages:
sara (support): Hey team — customer O11-ACCT reporting invoice spike vs dashboard. Invoice shows ~3.2k tokens for session, dashboard shows ~1.9k. Customer says they disconnected client mid-stream. Can we triage?

olle (customer): Confirmed — we hit cancel on the client around 13:42:07 UTC. Dashboard session id: s-9f3b. Invoice: INV-2026-1843. Looks like we were billed for extra ~1.3k tokens.

raj (billing): Thanks @sara / @olle. I pulled the ledger — I see two entries for the same request id (req-7a8c). One for 1,924 tokens and another for 1,300 tokens, posted ~3s apart. Both attributed to streaming generation.

zoe (eng-runtime): That pattern usually means the runtime emitted a final flush after the client disconnected and the streaming aggregator produced a second 'final' chunk that wasn't deduped. Do we have the raw SSE payloads?

olle (customer): We can share client logs. We see a network drop and then an immediate reconnect. Client printed: `SSE: got chunk id=42 size=420` then `connection closed by user`.

metering-bot: Recorded events for req-7a8c: [stream_start, chunk(42,420), chunk(43,1500), client_close], then [finalize_chunk(43,1300), stream_end].

zoe (eng-runtime): Aha — runtime emitted chunk 43 twice with different token counts (1500 vs 1300). Likely cause: during a partial flush the KV cache had tokens X, then reconciling/compaction trimmed whitespace which changed tokenization, then the finalize path emitted a corrected final chunk. Metering currently attributes both chunks to the same session because dedupe keys are per-chunk-seq, but they can be different on reflush.

raj (billing): Can we reconcile which tokens should be billable? Customer insists only one final chunk should count.

zoe (eng-runtime): Short repro: spin up local SSE client, send generation, interrupt TCP after partial payload, then server finalize on cleanup. Example logs:
```
[13:42:05.112] send chunk id=42 tokens=420 payload="..."
[13:42:07.021] client FIN received -> connection closed by client
[13:42:07.150] finalize triggered -> emit chunk id=43 tokens=1300 payload="..."
[13:42:07.153] reconcile -> previous chunk 43 (optimistic 1500) still in aggregator -> both persisted to ledger
```

zoe (eng-runtime): Repro steps I used: 1) start generate with SSE, 2) drop socket after first partial data frame, 3) call server-side cleanup which runs a tokenizer compaction pass and emits final chunk. That compaction can change token counts.

raj (billing): Proposed mitigation: billing should prefer the later finalize event but only if it shares an idempotency key or same chunk sequence. If sequences differ we need a policy: latest wins within 5s window for same session id, and mark earlier chunk as refunded in ledger.

sara (support): Would customer accept credit while we implement fix? Olle?

olle (customer): Yes please — we just want the extra charge removed while you investigate.

raj (billing): I'll file a manual adjustment for INV-2026-1843 and flag as refund_pending.

zoe (eng-runtime): Engineering next steps: 1) add stronger chunk dedupe using content-hash + seq id, 2) make finalize path emit an idempotency token `final_chunk_id` that meter can use, 3) add telemetry to surface compaction differences (old_count vs new_count). I'll open PR and link here.

sara (support): Thanks. Raj can you confirm when credit is applied? Zoe, please ping when PR is up.

raj (billing): Will update invoice status by EOD.

zoe (eng-runtime): PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/412 — adds final_chunk_id and a `compaction_delta` metric.

sara (support): resolving for now. follow-ups: eng to add dedupe, billing to refund, support to confirm with customer once refund posts. :white_check_mark:

olle (customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround.

metering-bot: Logged follow-up tasks: TASK-3342 (dedupe), TASK-3343 (ledger-refund), TASK-3344 (telemetry).
